title: Dynamic quota-aware tiered routing for request prioritization across regions and model fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a unified runtime policy that routes incoming inference requests by customer tier (free / paid / enterprise), respects per-tenant and global quotas, prefers lower-cost regions/models when appropriate, and gracefully falls back to compatible model variants when the preferred capacity is saturated. Current router treats tier as a static weight and doesn't combine quota exhaustion signals with region affinity; this leads to noisy failures for free tenants and unpredictable latency spikes for paid customers during regional contention.

Goal: Deliver a dynamic, quota-aware tiered routing mechanism that: (1) enforces per-tenant quota prioritization so enterprise traffic maintains SLOs when capacity is constrained, (2) routes to preferred region/model variants when latency/cost tradeoffs are favorable, (3) implements deterministic, auditable fallback chains for model variants, and (4) exposes observability to measure per-tier request drop rate, average latency, and cost impact.

Scope: Implement server-side logic in the gateway/router, add configuration surfaces in the control plane (routing policies and tier profiles), update the autoscaler to surface capacity signals, and add dashboards/alerts. This ticket covers design, an initial implementation behind a feature flag, integration tests, and a limited canary rollout for a subset of customers.

Non-goals: Full billing/chargeback changes, UI polish for the console, and advanced ML-driven dynamic weight tuning (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Router honors tier precedence so enterprise > paid > free when global GPU capacity is constrained
When a tenant's quota is exceeded the router applies soft-degradation (re-route to lower-cost region or smaller model) or hard-block based on tenant profile
Fallback policy supports at least three model variants per family and preserves semantic compatibility (same API surface)
Requests include a traceable routing decision with reason codes for audit (e.g., QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, REGION_AFFINITY, COST_OPTIMIZED)
Observability: dashboard shows per-tier throughput, drop/reject rates, average tail latency, and estimated token cost delta vs baseline
Feature can be toggled via a control-plane flag and rolled back without disrupting existing traffic
implementation_plan: Design: finalise policy DSL for tier profiles and fallback chains (this doc)
Router changes: add quota-check stage that is aware of per-tenant and per-tier buckets and returns ranked route candidates
Control plane: add REST endpoints to declare tier profiles and per-tenant soft/hard degrade behavior
Autoscaler signals: extend capacity API to publish per-region remaining QPS and model-variant capacity
Fallbacks: implement deterministic candidate selection logic including cost heuristics and model-compatibility checks
Observability: emit detailed routing events, add dashboard and alert rules
E2E tests: unit tests for decision logic, integration tests with local capacity simulator, canary on 2% of traffic for 72h
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Soft-degrade vs hard-block: prefer soft-degrade for paid tiers (re-route or smaller model) and hard-block only for free tier when quota is exhausted to protect paying customers
Tokenized quota model: use token-based token-bucket per-tenant for fine-grained control; simplified request-count quotas considered but rejected for precision
Region affinity: prefer region-local routing where latency SLOs are at risk; otherwise allow cost-optimized routing to lower-cost regions if tenant policy permits
Fallback determinism: deterministic ordering (priority list) chosen over probabilistic weighted routing to make audits and debugging straightforward
Backpressure handling: router will surface soft backpressure signals to the autoscaler, rather than immediately dropping traffic, to avoid oscillations
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Global quota enforcement latency could add to request path. Mitigation: cache quota decisions per-second and use local token-bucket fast-path in gateway

Risk: Re-routing to different regions might violate data residency constraints. Mitigation: use tenant policy flags to opt out of inter-region routing and enforce hard constraints for regulated tenants
Risk: Smaller model fallback could produce quality regressions. Mitigation: restrict model fallbacks per tenant; require 'accepts_smaller_model' flag and add quality-monitoring evals

Risk: Priority starvation if enterprise traffic consistently fills capacity. Mitigation: implement graceful degradation for enterprise via micro-shares + scheduled maintenance windows and capacity reservations
metrics_and_sla_targets: Per-tier success rate >= 99.5% for enterprise during normal load
Tail latency (p95) for paid tier <= 200ms on region-local routing
Fallback-induced quality regressions monitored via daily eval set and thresholded regression alerts
Route-change audit logs emitted for 100% of rerouted or rejected requests
testing_plan: Unit: decision engine tests for quota exhaustion, priority rules, and fallback ordering
Simulated-load integration tests: run orchestrated multi-region capacity simulator with mixed tier traffic to validate routing decisions
Canary: enable feature for small set of internal tenants and 2% of production traffic; compare SLOs and cost deltas for 72h
Chaos: simulate region outage and verify deterministic fallback chains keep enterprise traffic within SLOs
Perf: ensure decision latency added by router stage < 5ms p95
deployment_and_rollout: Canary: internal customers (team traffic) for 48h -> 2% external for 72h -> 20% for 7 days -> full rollout
Monitor: custom dashboard and PagerDuty rule for per-tier error increases or abnormal route divergence
Rollback: feature-flag immediately flips to fallback deterministic router; automated rollback if enterprise success rate drops >0.5%
notes: 2025-02-20: Spike completed; prototype router returns ranked candidate list with reason codes (Aisha)
